correctness.rationale: For x on a projectively fixed line with Mv^[2]=lambda v, the only nonzero solution on the line is lambda^(-1)v, and invertibility ensures lambda is nonzero. The binary cubic is not identically zero, hence has at most three distinct projective roots. Uniform invertible matrices induce uniform projectivities. For each ordered distinct tuple of size 1, 2 or 3, the incidence probability is the reciprocal of the number of such tuples if the square images are distinct and zero otherwise. In odd characteristic there are q-1 colliding ordered pairs and 3(q-1)^2 excluded ordered triples, counted once each; in even characteristic squaring is bijective. Factorial-moment inversion gives the stated table including q=2. The independent bounded enumeration solved the original algebra equations for every invertible matrix over F_2,F_3,F_4,F_5 and obtained the frozen histograms. The frozen verifier was read but not run; neither enumeration proves the theorem for all q.

evidence: Rank-one M gives the factorization (u_1 Y-u_2 X)(v_1 X^2+v_2 Y^2) for M=u v^T. Thus all root-free projective cubics occur on the invertible locus and, since infinity cannot be a root, normalize bijectively to irreducible monic cubics. Elements of F_(q^3) outside F_q contribute one per free three-element Frobenius orbit, giving (q^3-q)/3 versus q^3-q projective invertible matrices.

For odd q, projective cubics having exactly two rational roots are L^2 M with unequal linear factors, hence q(q+1) of them. Among rank-one forms, the diagonal quadratic either has a double root at an axis (2q choices with a different linear factor) or has an opposite nonzero split pair (q-1 choices when the linear factor is one of the pair). These disjoint cases exhaust deletions, leaving (q-1)^2 invertible projective cubics with two distinct roots. This gives exactly the advertised odd P2. Normalization, the first moment and N<=3 then determine the other probabilities.

originality.rationale: The earlier field-independent characteristic-two record gives the even row exactly, and the universal headline one-third is mechanically the classical irreducible-cubic count: every projective cubic with no rational root belongs to the invertible matrix locus because rank-one matrices yield a rational linear factor. For odd q the remaining independent stratum N=2 is obtained by ordinary split-cubic factor counts with a rank-one deletion, detailed below; the prior first moment and P0 then determine the rest. Two later-dated indexed statements exactly match the full distribution; this is separate evidence of equivalence, not proof that either had priority. The rejection is not a claim that the odd row was found explicitly in an earlier paper.
residual_risks: The bounded search does not determine historical priority for the explicit full table. The later date of an equivalent catalogue entry neither proves nor rules out earlier publication elsewhere.

value.rationale: Uniform matrix weighting is natural, and a genuinely unknown law here could be valuable. As frozen, the even row is an earlier explicit specialization, the headline is a textbook root-free cubic count on the invertible locus, and the odd correction is a direct rank-one deletion from a standard splitting count. The exact probabilities are correct but do not leave a distinct mathematical result substantial enough for a repair.
